name: Mandorla - Coloring Page Generator for Unity
summary: Generates coloring and colour-by-number pages from a seed: line art, numbers, a reference fill, a region map and one white piece per area. It converts your own line art too.
description:
Coloring pages for your coloring or colour-by-number game, generated in the editor from any seed.

Coloring templates are engines. They ship a handful of pictures, and every page after that is yours to draw and slice by hand. Mandorla generates the pages. Pick a family and a seed and it draws a closed-region page, finds every colourable area the way a flood fill in your game will find it, numbers the areas, colours a reference version, and writes everything into your project in the format sliced templates load. Any integer is a seed, so the next page is always one click away. It also converts your own clean line art into the same outputs.

SIX HAND-AUTHORED FAMILIES

Mandala: concentric bands of petals, scallops, cells, beads and zigzags around a centre flower, with a pointed crown.
Rosette: a flower-of-life centre inside rings of beads and a scalloped crown.
Lattice: eight-point stars in an octagon-and-square net, or hexagrams in a hexagon net, framed.
Stained Glass: a leaded arch window of jittered glass cells with a centre medallion.
Botanical: a radial wreath with a layered centre bloom, stems with veined leaves, blooms and buds.
Zentangle: curved strings divide a framed page and each area gets its own tangle pattern.

Detail 1 to 5 sets how busy a page is. Measured over ten seeds per family, the average page grows from 107 to 392 areas on Mandala, 120 to 680 on Lattice and 89 to 340 on Zentangle. Eight reference palettes (Sunset, Tidepool, Meadow, Jewel, Pastel, Autumn, Berry, Desert) colour areas that belong together alike and keep neighbours apart where the palette allows it.

WHAT ONE EXPORT WRITES

Each page gets its own folder: line.png and line_transparent.png (the line art on paper and on transparency), reference.png (the reference fill), numbered.png (the colour-by-number page), regions.png (each pixel stores area id + 1 in red and green, imported uncompressed and readable, so a tap is one texel read), page.json (every area's id, number, pixel area, bounds, deepest point and inscribed radius) and a pieces folder with one white sprite per area, the separate white parts format sliced coloring templates load. Export N seeds writes a whole batch in one press.

SAFE TO FILL, BY CONSTRUCTION

Areas are found on the raster you export, 4-connected, at the page's own resolution. The test suite floods the exported line.png from every area and requires each fill to stay inside its area. A child-safe floor makes every area hold a circle of a size you choose; an area too small to tap is inked solid instead of shipped as a speck. The same options always give byte-identical pages.

YOUR OWN LINE ART

The Convert line art tab takes any texture, readable or not. Mandorla finds every closed area, seals small breaks in the outlines and draws each seal into the line layer, so the boundary a fill stops at is always visible. Conversion needs clean line art: dark lines on a light or transparent ground.

GETTING STARTED

1. Import the package. Everything lands under Assets/CSAF/Mandorla/.
2. Open Demo/Scenes/MandorlaDemo.unity and press Play: a small colour-by-number game built on the included ColoringBoard. Pick a colour (click a swatch or press 1 to 8) and click an area.
3. Open Window > CSAF > Mandorla, choose a family, seed and detail, and press Generate.
4. Press Export this page, or Export N seeds, into the export folder (default Assets/Mandorla Pages).
technical:
Features: closed-region coloring pages generated from a family and a seed; six hand-authored families; detail 1 to 5; eight reference palettes; numbered colour-by-number overlay; region map; one white sprite piece per area; page.json metadata; child-safe floor with an ink warning; conversion of your own line art with gap sealing; ColoringBoard for playing a page; editor window with batch export.

Number of C# scripts: 12 (10 Runtime, 1 Editor, 1 Demo). Visual Scripting graphs: 0.
Assemblies: CSAF.Mandorla.Runtime (all platforms), CSAF.Mandorla.Editor (Editor only), CSAF.Mandorla.Demo (demo scene).
Editor window: Window > CSAF > Mandorla. Demo scene: Assets/CSAF/Mandorla/Demo/Scenes/MandorlaDemo.unity.
Minimum Unity version: 2022.3. Built and tested against 6000.5.7f1.
Render pipelines: Built-in, URP and HDRP. Pages are drawn on the CPU into textures.
Input: the demo reads input through Event.current, so it also runs in projects set to the Input System package only.
Target platforms: plain C# runtime with no native code. The demo generates with Task.Run, which needs threads (not tested on WebGL).
No Resources folder, no shaders, no images, no fonts, no audio, no network calls. Dependencies: none.
No third-party assets are included.

Documentation: https://github.com/onefreeman1337/csaf-releases/blob/main/docs/mandorla/README.md
ai:
All of the C# in this package was written by an AI coding agent (Anthropic Claude) under human direction. That covers the six page families, the region finder, the palette assignment, the line art converter, the ColoringBoard, the editor window and the demo scene.

The pages the package produces are not made by an image model. Every line is drawn by the shipped code from authored families, and the numbers are drawn from figures in the package. The store images are captures and composites of that output. The store cover uses an AI-generated illustration of a desk as its background, with a real Mandorla page laid on it.

No audio is included, because the package contains no audio of any kind. Text and dialog: no.
